nodes.name: Theorem D
nodes.statement:
Let $k_0$ be an infinite perfect field of characteristic $\neq \ell$.
  Let $K_0$ be a regular function field over $k_0$ of transcendence degree $\geq 5$, and put $K = K_0 \cdot k$.
  Let $\mathbf{a}$ be an arbitrary (possibly-empty) finite tuple of elements of $k_0^\times$.
  Then the canonical map
  \[ \rho^{\rm M}_{k_0,K_0} : {\mathrm{Gal}_{k_0}} \rightarrow \underline{\mathrm{Aut}}^{\rm M}_{\mathbf{a}}(\operatorname{k}^{\rm M}_1(K)) \]
  is an isomorphism.

nodes.name: Theorem C
nodes.statement:
Let $k_0$ be an infinite perfect field of characteristic $\neq \ell$.
  Let $K_0$ be a regular function field over $k_0$ of transcendence degree $\geq 5$, and put $K = K_0 \cdot k$.
  Let $\mathbf{a}$ be an arbitrary (possibly-empty) finite tuple of elements of $k_0^\times$.
  Then the canonical map
  \[ \rho_{k_0} : {\mathrm{Gal}_{k_0}} \rightarrow \underline{\mathrm{Aut}}^{\rm c}_{\mathbf{a}}(\mathcal{G}_K^a) \]
  is an isomorphism.

nodes.name: Theorem A
nodes.statement:
Let $k_0$ be an infinite perfect field of characteristic $\neq \ell$.
  Let $\mathcal{U}$ be a birational system of dimension $\geq 5$, and let $\mathbf{a} = (a_1,\ldots,a_r)$ be a (possibly empty) finite tuple of elements of $k_0^\times$.
  Then the canonical Galois representation 
  \[ \rho^c_{k_0,\mathcal{U}_{\mathbf{a}}} : {\mathrm{Gal}_{k_0}} \rightarrow \underline{\mathrm{Aut}}^{\rm c}(\pi^a|_{\mathcal{U}_{\mathbf{a}}}) \]
  is an isomorphism.

nodes.name: Theorem B
nodes.statement:
Let $k_0$ be an infinite perfect field of characteristic $\neq \ell$, and let $\mathcal{V}$ be a subcategory of $\mathbf{Var}_{k_0}$ which is $5$-connected.
  Then the canonical Galois representation 
  \[ \rho^c_{k_0,\mathcal{V}} : {\mathrm{Gal}_{k_0}} \rightarrow \underline{\mathrm{Aut}}^{\rm c}(\pi^a|_{\mathcal{V}}) \]
  is an isomorphism.

nodes.name: Theorem 4.2
nodes.statement:
The following hold:
  \begin{enumerate}
    \item Let $\phi \in \mathrm{Aut}(\operatorname{k}^{\rm M}_1(K))$ be given and consider $\phi^* \in \mathrm{Aut}(\mathcal{G}_K^a)$ the Kummer-dual of $\phi$.
    Then one has $\phi \in \mathrm{Aut}^{\rm M}(\operatorname{k}^{\rm M}_1(K))$ if and only if $\phi^* \in \mathrm{Aut}^{\rm c}(\mathcal{G}_K^a)$.
    \item The canonical isomorphism $\mathcal{K} : \mathrm{Aut}(\mathcal{G}_K^a) \xrightarrow{\cong} \mathrm{Aut}(\operatorname{k}^{\rm M}_1(K))$ restricts to an isomorphism $\mathcal{K} : \mathrm{Aut}^{\rm c}(\mathcal{G}_K^a) \xrightarrow{\cong} \mathrm{Aut}^{\rm M}(\operatorname{k}^{\rm M}_1(K))$.
    \item The canonical isomorphism $\mathcal{K} : \underline{\mathrm{Aut}}(\mathcal{G}_K^a) \xrightarrow{\cong} \underline{\mathrm{Aut}}(\operatorname{k}^{\rm M}_1(K))$ restricts to an isomorphism $\mathcal{K} : \underline{\mathrm{Aut}}^{\rm c}(\mathcal{G}_K^a) \xrightarrow{\cong} \underline{\mathrm{Aut}}^{\rm M}(\operatorname{k}^{\rm M}_1(K))$ which is compatible with $\rho_{k_0}$.
  \end{enumerate}
